candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide client education that promotes preventive self-care and reduces risk of chronic-disease complications
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive diabetic foot self-care
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with diabetic neuropathy or loss of protective sensation to inspect their feet every day so painless skin injuries or preulcerative changes can be identified and treated early.

options.A: Inspect both feet every day, including the soles and between the toes, because neuropathy can allow minor injuries to go unnoticed; use a mirror or ask for help if needed.
options.B: Check the feet only after walking long distances because painless injuries are unlikely during normal daily activity.
options.C: Rely on pain to identify early ulcers because diabetic neuropathy usually increases sensitivity to foot injury.
options.D: Inspect the feet once a month unless an open wound is already visible.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend daily surveillance for early foot problems, particularly in people with loss of protective sensation, using visual inspection, palpation, or an unbreakable mirror when needed. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy can reduce or eliminate protective pain sensation, allowing minor trauma to go unrecognized and progress to ulceration or infection. B, C, and D delay detection and incorrectly rely on pain or infrequent inspection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Loss of protective sensation can make foot trauma painless or unrecognized, and current ADA guidance recommends daily foot surveillance for early problems, with mirror or caregiver assistance when needed.
candidate.source_document_title: Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Foot Care Recommendations 12.25 and 12.30; ‘Foot Care Education for People With Diabetes’ — people with sensory loss should have feet inspected at every visit and receive education on daily surveillance using palpation or visual inspection with an unbreakable mirror; LOPS predisposes to unrecognized minor trauma and diabetic foot ulceration
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client with diabetes and loss of protective sensation in both feet says, “I only check my feet when they hurt.” Which response by the nurse is best?
